newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Firestone sees good demand in second half.
newsitem.headline: Firestone sees good demand in second half.

text.p: Tyre manufacturer Firestone New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday that despite some difficulties, strong demand augured well for the second half of the year.

"Firestone has countered the negative effects in the New Zealand market with a complete re-image of its retail network and a commitment to upgrading stores which has had a positive effect on business," the company said.
"In spite of the pressures and difficulties faced by the company, there continues to be a strong demand for Firestone products which augurs well for the second half."

The company said a slowing economy, squeezed margins from increased competition and local production difficulties saw its first half net profit fall to $2.18 million from $2.45 million a year earlier.
It had taken measures to meet greater competition from lower priced products both in the domestic market and in Australia during the first half of the year.
While this helped Firestone lift sales revenues 3.7 percent to $60.6 million and improve unit sales by 4.5 percent, "these results came at a cost", it said.
Firestone had to contend with some problems at the Christchurch manufacturing plant earlier in the year which affected productivity.

Pressures also continued from lower tariffs and the higher number of imports of used tyres and cars, resulting in a decision by Ford and Mazda to close down their assembly plant in 1997 and impacting on their decision to make Firestone their sole tyre supplier.
Firestone declared a fully imputed dividend of 10 cents per share -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
